high_risk_moment: After the virtual teaching assistant receives a question that is ambiguous or outside its validated course scope
stakeholder: Artificial intelligence student relying on an autonomous course response
harm_description: An incorrect or out-of-scope answer can reinforce a misconception about AI concepts or course requirements and delay access to appropriate human clarification.
existing_controls: Jill Watson augmented human teachers and its reported autonomous duties were bounded to introductions, announcements, and routine frequently asked questions; the source does not provide a production error-rate estimate.
proposed_controls: Require instructor-approved AI course sources and worked reasoning, pre-release topic evaluation, visible grounding references, uncertainty disclosure, and abstention with teaching-assistant escalation when a supported answer cannot be produced.
human_oversight: The AI Course Content Lead approves the source and reasoning set before release; a teaching assistant reviews every reported error within one business day and can withdraw an answer, disable a topic, or pause the tutor while evidence is reviewed.
monitoring_metric: Confirmed factual or conceptual error rate in a stratified weekly sample of released answers by AI-course topic
trigger_threshold: More than 1% confirmed errors in a weekly sample or any error that materially misstates a foundational AI concept, evaluation result, model limitation, bias risk, or responsible-use safeguard
response_action: Pause the affected topic, switch learners to instructor-approved static guidance, preserve review records, correct the content, and require instructor re-test before re-enabling it.

high_risk_moment: During tutoring after a student submits a coding or AI-course help request
stakeholder: Student who receives confusing guidance or relies on the tutor instead of performing the reasoning
harm_description: Misunderstood requests or guidance using untaught concepts can confuse novice learners, while overly convenient assistance can reduce productive struggle and create dependence without durable understanding.
existing_controls: CodeHelp used guardrails intended not to reveal solutions and complemented human support; the study also recorded student reports of confusing, unrelated, or out-of-syllabus advice and a small number of over-reliance concerns.
proposed_controls: Require an authentic student attempt before hints, reveal support progressively, constrain guidance to approved course concepts, prompt the student to explain each step, and route misunderstood or repeated direct-answer requests to human support.
human_oversight: The Learning Experience Owner defines the pedagogical policy; lecturers review weekly learning, confusion, and bypass indicators, while teaching assistants can intervene in flagged sessions and the owner can disable affected paths.
monitoring_metric: Confusing or out-of-syllabus response rate, hint-to-solution bypass rate, and post-practice mastery for repeated tutor users
trigger_threshold: More than 2% confirmed confusing or out-of-syllabus responses, more than 10% of weekly sessions reaching a complete solution without a recorded student attempt, or pilot mastery declining for two consecutive reviews
response_action: Restrict the affected flow, require an intermediate reasoning step, offer human tutoring, investigate the content and interaction design, and re-test learning outcomes before restoring the flow.

high_risk_moment: When a request is made to reuse tutor interactions or generated text for grading or academic-integrity review
stakeholder: Student whose writing or tutor log is repurposed without being the decision-system customer
harm_description: Repurposing tutor logs or generated-text signals as evidence of misconduct can disproportionately flag non-native English writers, expose learning data, and lead to false accusation, dignity loss, or unequal educational treatment.
existing_controls: AIGuide's approved scope excludes grading and misconduct detection; the cited institution disabled AI detection and recommended direct educator-student review instead of relying on detector output.
proposed_controls: Prohibit AI-authorship scores and disciplinary exports, enforce purpose-limited access to tutor logs, require a new impact and legal review for any assessment use, and maintain notice, contestability, and an appeal path for affected students.
human_oversight: The Academic Integrity Lead must reject any AI-only referral; if a scoped human review is legally authorized, an independent educator examines original work and context, notifies the student, records the rationale, and has authority to overturn or halt the process.
monitoring_metric: Count of AI-only disciplinary referrals and attempts to export tutor data for grading or misconduct decisions
trigger_threshold: Any AI-only referral or any unauthorized secondary-use export attempt
response_action: Block the integration, suspend the requesting access, notify the Product Owner and privacy reviewer, review any affected decisions, provide appeal and correction, and re-classify the product before considering the new use.
